patch.value: Harden credential_key_assignment and URL-userinfo redaction against adversarial spellings found after PR 1712

PR 1712 (pm-gh1704, pm-gh1707) ran about fifteen adversarial review rounds (Codex, CodeRabbit, Greptile). Every reported escape inside the GH-1704 table and the GH-1707 shapes was fixed and pinned in the specs, but each round produced new, increasingly exotic spellings, so the loop was stopped with these known residuals. (1) Unquoted values after a colon or a spaced equals sign that contain ? : or | (client_secret: q7!A?9#z) are read as code, a deliberate trade-off with JavaScript optional chains. (2) The GH-1699 escaped-literal decoder swaps the literal's own quote kind for the other one before the entropy predicate runs, so an escaped JSON value holding both quote kinds can measure below the threshold. (3) Detection is heuristic by construction. Next steps: a declared adversarial corpus with a measured escape rate next to the false-positive corpus of pm-1l85at, an entropy predicate that judges the decoded original rather than the neutralized literal, and a case-sensitive context check for env-style lines (KEY: value with an all-caps key).

A declared adversarial corpus with a measured escape rate exists for credential_key_assignment and URL-userinfo redaction; Escaped JSON literals are judged for entropy on their decoded original value; Env-style lines with an all-caps key detect unquoted credentials holding ? : or | without re-flagging code
New credential spellings are found by measurement, not by review rounds
Each review round found a new exotic spelling

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Residuals for the adversarial corpus, from the pm-ycgb5g and pm-3fbj1f review loop (Codex rounds 1 to 3, 2026-11-17). (1) password_assignment follows references nested one level in an unquoted value. A literal default nested three or more levels deep (password=${A:-${B:-${C:-<literal>}}}), or a literal after such a reference, is missed in the flat and quoted-key spellings, while quoted values and elements follow any depth through expandRuntimeReferences. Closing it needs a code tokenizer in place of the declared regex value grammar. (2) An unquoted password value may hold at most four whitespace-free quoted pieces; a literal spread over more pieces is missed. That bound keeps each structured scan to a few later keys. (3) A bare $VAR is still read as literal text by password_assignment and as a reference by credential_key_assignment; pm-hw00c2 owns aligning the two.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Progress from the pm-ycgb5g branch (not closing this item): the second criterion, judging escaped JSON literals on their decoded original, is implemented for every key-named rule. decodeQuotedLiteral returns both the neutralized reading the value grammar reads and the decoded original at the same length. Capture offsets (d flag) map the matched span back, and acceptsSecretMatch then judges the original, so credential_key_assignment measures entropy on the decoded original value. The other criteria remain open: a declared adversarial corpus with a measured escape rate, and env-style all-caps keys.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Residual (4), from the CodeRabbit review of PR 1745: an escaped quoted literal followed directly by an unquoted suffix in the same value (a quoted key whose value is an escaped literal glued to eight more literal characters) has only the escaped literal judged. The suffix is never measured, and the flat rule cannot match a quoted key. Main behaves the same. Closing it needs a mixed literal model: the decoded literal's characters are data and the suffix is text with shell quoting.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Residual (5), from the CodeRabbit review of PR 1745: a password value's quoted piece ends at its first closing quote, even inside a reference, and the cut reference contributes nothing. So in a double-quoted value that holds a command reference with its own double quotes, a literal after that inner quote is not measured. Closing it needs a quoted-value scan that follows references, done in code rather than by the declared regex grammar.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Residual (6), from the Greptile review of PR 1745: every repeated group of the password value grammar is bounded at 4096 iterations, so a value is read up to 4096 pieces (runs, references, quoted pieces). A literal placed after 4096 leading references is not judged. The bound keeps every scan stack-safe; unbounded, a value of millions of references overflows the backtrack stack and the guard fails open. Main never judged a literal after a reference at all, so this is a limit of the new check, not a regression. Closing it needs a scan in code that continues past the bound without reopening the cross-key cost the quoted-piece bound prevents.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Residuals (7) and (8), from the credential-key reference work (2026-11-17). (7) credential_key_assignment reads references and quoted pieces only when they are whitespace-free, as every credential-key value is. So a spaced command substitution followed directly by a literal is not judged under a credential key, while password_assignment, which allows spaced references, judges it. Spaced references stay excluded on purpose: a key inside a spaced command substitution then keeps its own verdict. (8) This predates the change and came with the whole-value password grammar: a password value that is a spaced command substitution is captured whole and spells nothing, so a password assignment written inside that command (an echo of another password key) is never visited. The main build before the whole-value grammar still visited the inner key. Closing it needs a bounded rescan of reference bodies after a rejected match: linear because reference nesting is bounded, but every key-named rule's flat scan would pay for it.

value.text: Residuals (8) and (9), from the CodeRabbit review of PR 1746 (2026-11-17); both are recorded limits, and main misses both. (8) credential_key_assignment rescans a rejected referenced value one level deep (shallow), so a referenced credential nested two command substitutions deep is judged only by the reference-free reading, which treats a dollar-led value as a placeholder. A deep rescan would be quadratic for entropy-rejected chains, because a credential key with its separator can be shorter than the literal minimum; closing it needs a depth-capped rescan with its own linear-time proof. (9) A credential-key value led by a lowercase dollar-name followed by a quoted literal keeps the reference-free reading, where a dollar-led literal is a placeholder. Only CONSTANT_CASE names are read as leading references. Closing it would mean judging the literal with the leading name removed for the grammar but kept for length and entropy; each such widening needs its own false-positive measurement over the tracker corpus first (pm-1l85at).

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Residuals (10) to (12), from the Greptile review of PR 1746 (2026-11-17); main behaves the same in all three. (10) A credential-key literal after a reference that ends with an opening parenthesis is read as a call and not judged; the shape is indistinguishable from a function call in source text. (11) A command substitution whose inner option name is quoted is visited by the structured pass as a quoted key, outside the rescan's enclosing-reference context, so a bare variable there keeps main's literal reading and is reported. (12) Inside a command substitution, a closing brace after a quoted inner variable is taken for the reference's own delimiter, so a literal suffix glued after it is not judged. Closing (11) and (12) needs the enclosing reference boundary carried into every match a rescan or structured walk makes inside a rejected value.

value.text: Residuals (13) and (14), from the Greptile review of PR 1746; main judges neither shape, because it treats every dollar-led credential-key value as a placeholder. (13) After a reference, an exclamation mark followed by a dot, an operator or a call reads as a TypeScript non-null assertion, so a YAML literal that starts with those characters right after a reference is not judged. (14) In the referenced reading each single ampersand is its own piece, so with more than 2,048 single ampersands the value is read only up to the 4,096-piece bound, the same stack-safety bound as residual (6) for the password grammar.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Residual (15), from the CodeRabbit review of PR 1746: an escaped dollar sign in a decoded string literal decodes to a dollar sign, so a whole-value escaped variable reads as a bare variable and is a placeholder. A shell reader would keep that dollar literal, but a JavaScript string or template literal yields the plain dollar sign; preserving the escape flagged template-literal fixtures with escaped interpolation. Closing it needs the host language of the surrounding text.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Residual (16), from Codex review round 34 on PR 1746: some credential-key exclusion patterns (hyphenated words, paths, unquoted member chains) still exhaust the regex stack on values of millions of characters, as they already did in 2026.11.17. Since PR 1746 such a value fails closed for itself (reported under the rule with normalization_incomplete) instead of failing the whole scan open. Making those exclusions stack-safe, for example by scanning them in code, would remove the review noise for such values.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Residuals (17) to (20), from the pm-gh1775 and pm-gh1773 work (2026-11-23); main behaves the same or worse in each. (17) In serialized JSON text, a credential-key literal attached to a dollar-name reference behind an ESCAPED quote (the JSON spelling of a shell concatenation inside a string value) is not judged: the flat grammar reads raw text, where the backslash ends the value, and the structured pass judges only quoted-key values. The 2026.11.23 build misses it too. (18) Prose that quotes a whole password assignment ending in a CONSTANT_CASE dollar-name, followed by a space and more prose, is still reported by password_assignment, because a quote then a spaced word may open a shell piece holding a passphrase; only a quote followed by a line break, the end of the text, or JSON structure and the next member ends the word. Flagged on 2026.11.14 as well. (19) A structure-only quoted piece (comma, colon, braces, brackets) followed by a string that closes on the same line is now a string boundary in both key-named grammars, so a deliberate shell concatenation of a reference, a quoted comma and a quoted literal is not reported; the same text without the closing quote still is. (20) URL userinfo that holds whitespace is joined across words only when the opening word carries a user-colon prefix (a colon that port digits alone never follow) and the at sign or its escape follows within 16 words and 512 code units; a whitespace-bearing bare token and a numeric password that looks like a port are still split.

(18) A value that sits in a string now ends at that string's closing quote when JSON structure and the next member, a blank, or the end of the text follow it, so a shell concatenation of a reference with a quoted comma piece written INSIDE a string (echo, a quoted reference, a closing quote, a comma, a quoted literal) is not reported; the same shape outside every string still is. (20) A Windows percent-name under a password key is still read as literal text (flagged before 2026.11.14 too); a percent-name-prefixed literal under a credential key is excluded by the reference-free grammar's placeholder prefix (main as well). (21) A credential URL followed within 16 words by prose holding an at sign (an email) is redacted through that at sign, as a URL parser reads the authority; prose context there is lost, never a credential.
